messages:
Rina: Quick thought  can we add a "quickapply" action to rollout playbooks that does a stepped-degrade (10% -> 30% -> 60%) automatically with cooldowns? Mock here: https://figma.com/proto/quickapply-stepper
Jon: Love the idea. Helps avoid a hard redirect. Need to show exact timing & hysteresis. How do we surface rollback reasons in the UI?
Sam: Stepped-degrade OK but we need an escape hatch. If error rate increases after a step, we should stop escalation and either hold or roll back depending on config.
Priya: Proposal: name the feature "stepped-degrade quickapply" and expose parameters: steps[], step_duration, escalation_on_worsen (bool), rollback_threshold. UI shows an inline preview of traffic curve and est token delta.
Tomas: Telemetry: emit `stepped_degrade_decision_v1` with decision_id, route, steps, operator, sampled_traces flag. Header: `X-Fallback-Token: <uuid>` for trace joins. Keep sampled traces for 2% while active.
Rina: Also show a small cost estimator per-step and an overall safety leash (max tokens/24h). If leash is hit, stop further steps and notify the inbox.
Jon: RBAC: quickapply apply rights limited to senior oncall. Others can simulate and queue requests for approval. Record free-text reason on apply.
Sam: Backend: scheduler that executes steps and evaluates signals between steps. Add cooldown windows to avoid flip-flop.
Priya: UX: confirmation modal that lists steps, expected reduction per-step, est. cost, and a "dry-run (shadow)" checkbox. Dry-run does shadow routing and shows live diff for one step period.
ops-bot: ops-bot: rolling canary completed (sha=ccf9ae) no stepped-degrade triggers during canary
Tomas: I'll draft proto + BigQuery mapping. Use decision_id to link to request logs. Will open PR with sampling knobs.
Rina: Cool. I'll add quickapply to the playbook mock and include copy for the confirmation modal. Thanks all.
